analysis.investment_thesis: Nazara rides India's real gaming and esports structural tailwind with 25.5% revenue CAGR, but the serial-acquisition model has produced near-zero operating margins (1.98%), ROE of 2.9%, and negative FCF in FY25 — value is being consumed, not created. At 133x P/E for a business earning INR 51 Cr net profit on INR 1,624 Cr revenue, the market is pricing perfection into a deeply imperfect business.
key_strengths: India gaming/esports structural tailwind — underpenetrated market with genuine 10-year runway
High gross margins of 71% confirm platform-model economics are theoretically sound
Revenue scaled 8x in 9 years (INR 211 Cr → INR 1,624 Cr) and EBITDA trend is expanding
key_risks: Profitability destruction: Net profit CAGR of -2.7% over 9 years despite 25.5% revenue growth — INR 51 Cr profit in FY25 is lower than FY2016's INR 65 Cr
Capital-hungry acquisition machine: investing CF was -INR 1,139 Cr in FY25 alone, FCF turned negative (-INR 82 Cr), and financing CF of +INR 805 Cr means constant equity dilution
Chronic ROE/ROCE of ~2.5-3% — far below cost of capital, meaning every rupee of equity raised destroys shareholder value at current execution
red_flags: Net profit declined from INR 75 Cr (FY24) to INR 51 Cr (FY25) despite 43% revenue growth — acquisitions are dilutive
Other income of INR 80 Cr nearly equals operating income of INR 115 Cr — core operations barely profitable
Promoter holding at just 35.45% — low skin in the game for a promoter-driven India story
Massive equity raises (reserves up INR 1,353 Cr YoY) continuously dilute minorities with no earnings leverage to show for it
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Nazara is a roll-up of gaming assets — esports (NODWIN), fantasy sports, casual mobile, adtech, and media — stitched together across India, Africa, and globally. The 71% gross margin looks seductive, but enormous acquisition amortization, content costs, and integration expenses drag operating margins to a pitiful 1.98%. The business has now crossed INR 1,600 Cr in revenue and still cannot generate meaningful bottom-line profit. FY25 net profit of INR 51 Cr on INR 1,624 Cr revenue implies a net margin of just 3.1% — and that *includes* INR 80 Cr of other income (investment/treasury gains). Strip that out and core operations are essentially breakeven.

From my investing lens, the cardinal sin here is capital destruction. ROE of 2.9% and ROCE of 2.5% on a market cap of INR 10,126 Cr is disqualifying. The company spent INR 1,139 Cr on investments in FY25 and raised INR 805 Cr in financing — this is a machine that consumes capital, not generates it. P/E at 133x for this quality of earnings is not a growth premium; it is speculation. I love India's gaming story deeply, but I want companies that translate the story into rupees of earnings per share. Nazara has not done that in 9 years of trying. The sector is right, the execution and capital discipline are not. Pass.
